text:
anna_support: Hey team, ACME reporting intermittent 502s from hosted API over the last 30m after they rotated service tokens. Error rate ~5-8% across a few regions. They have a repro curl.
acme_ops: @anna_support yes, started right after token rotate. curl + response attached: 
acme_ops: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <new-token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer <new-token>
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 16
> 
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"upstream connection reset"}
```
anna_support: They see it across small/large requests, streaming and non-streaming. Can we triage?
josh_eng: grabbing traces now — can you share a trace-id when it happened? any X-Request-ID?
acme_ops: one example: req-id=acme-1681234-7, region=us-west-2, time=2023-04-12T14:02:31Z
maria_sre: checking proxy metrics for that window. quick note: no deploys around that time. Envoy upstream_reset rate spiked on a subset of front-door nodes.
maria_sre: looks like reset counts correlate with connections that had no SNI in the TLS ClientHello — suspicious.
kevin_se: Wait, why would client lose SNI? They are using our SDK which delegates to standard TLS stack. They only rotated tokens.
josh_eng: hypothesis: token rotation triggered client reconnects from new worker that doesn't set TLS SNI due to a platform change (we've seen older TLS lib on some hosts omit SNI when using raw sockets). If TLS handshake lacks SNI, our LB routing hits default_vhost which points to an internal placeholder cluster that rejects with 502.
anna_support: That would match customer timeline (rotation caused short-lived pool churn). Any logs validating missing SNI?
maria_sre: pulled pcap from one front-door host for that minute — several ClientHello without server_name extension. Example: 
<maria_sre> TLS ClientHello: version=1.2, extensions=[ec_point_formats, supported_groups] (no server_name)
acme_ops: we can repro by spawning multiple workers and rotating tokens rapidly. customer willing to test a workaround.
kevin_se: Proposed mitigations: 1) Advise customers to use SDK versions with modern TLS (quick). 2) Default LB should handle no-SNI gracefully (longer infra change) — route by Host header fallback instead of default cluster. 3) Short-term: add 5xx-resilient retry in our gateway for no-sni case (automatic 1 retry).
josh_eng: also adding traffic-rule to direct no-sni connections to a healthy cluster that responds with 421 or a nicer error instead of 502 until we fix routing.
maria_sre: I'll open infra ticket to update Envoy config: enable sni_fallback to host_header routing and log occurrences.
maria_sre: ticket INF-2023-481 created, patch queued for canary tomorrow.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: infra/inf-proxy patch canary -> 2023-04-13 03:00 UTC (rollout 5% first).
anna_support: For customer: asked ACME to enable SDK flag to force SNI (they confirmed their clients can flip to newer TLS stack, testing now).
acme_ops: testing now — flip to v2 SDK, running rotate sequence again. Will report in 10m.
acme_ops: update: after v2 SDK, no 502s in 20m window. Looks fixed on their side.
anna_support: Great — asked them to hold rotation cadence until canary lands. Also gave them temporary retry advice.
kevin_se: Next steps: infra change to add host_header fallback, monitor no-sni metric, add product doc note about older TLS stacks and token rotations.
josh_eng: logging todo: emit a clear metric 'frontdoor.no_sni_count' tagged by region and node. Alert if >0.5% of requests for 5m.
maria_sre: will add that to INF-2023-481.
anna_support: Closing loop with ACME, will ship summary and recommended SDK upgrade + timeline for infra fix. :thumbsup:
acme_ops: thanks all, huge help.
anna_support: marking as resolved for now, reopen if they see new failures.
